slides.title: Sample Deck: Schema Conformance Fixture
slides.subtitle: Exercises every layout in presentation2/SCHEMA.md
slides.notes: This is the build's own test fixture, not part of the physics talk. It exists so verify_presentation2.py can build a real deck end to end -- validate the section JSON, generate a figure, render an equation to a PNG, emit both the pptx and the html, and run the office-validate schema check -- without depending on the four content workers' section files, which are written concurrently and may not exist yet or may still contain schema errors while they are drafted. Every layout the schema defines appears somewhere in this thirteen-slide fixture, including the two newest additions, equation+figure and bullets+table, so a single build of this file alone exercises every renderer code path the real talk will eventually use, section by section, layout by layout.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Bullets layout
bullets: Up to six bullets, each at most about eighteen words long
Plain text bullets render as-is in both the slide deck and the web page
An inline $E=\hbar\omega$ math snippet stays as text, not an image
$\Gamma = 1/\tau$
slides.notes: Demonstrates the plain bullets layout, including the schema's inline-math rule: a bullet that mixes ordinary words with dollar-delimited math stays plain text in both renderers, while a bullet that is only a dollar-delimited expression on its own is rendered as an equation image in the pptx, because pptxgenjs cannot rasterize LaTeX inline the way a real slide would want it to look. The html renderer never rasterizes math at all, by design -- it is MathJax-free, so every math snippet, whether mixed with words or standing alone, is wrapped in a monospace span and shown as literal text instead of typeset symbols, keeping the web page dependency-free and fast to load with no network access.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Bullets + figure layout
bullets: Bullets on one side, a generated figure on the other
The figure is a PNG produced by a re-runnable, deterministic script
Figures are never downloaded, only generated at build time

equations.caption: total decay rate; Gamma_rad radiative rate, Gamma_nr non-radiative rate

slides.notes: Demonstrates the combined bullets+figure layout: bullet text on one side of the slide, the referenced figure and its caption on the other, sized so neither column crowds the other. This slide also now carries an equations array -- a schema-wide rule change requires every layout that has an equations array to render those equations somewhere on the slide, not only the dedicated equation layout, so sections written by other workers do not silently lose their formulas just because the author chose a bullets+figure or table layout instead. Here the renderer places the equation in a compact strip beneath the bullets and figure, exercising exactly that new rule end to end, alongside the figure-generation and bullets-column code paths this layout has always tested.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Figure-only layout

figure.caption: The same sample figure, shown large with no competing text

slides.notes: Demonstrates the figure-only layout: a large centered figure with a caption and a short title, no bullet text competing for attention. This layout is meant for a single diagram, plot, or schematic that deserves the whole slide -- a device cross-section, a level diagram, a measured or simulated trace -- where accompanying prose belongs in the speaker notes rather than on the slide itself. The fixture reuses the same synthetic damped-oscillation figure as the bullets+figure slide above, produced by the same deterministic, re-runnable matplotlib script, so this check never has to generate a second image just to exercise the figure-only code path in both renderers, keeping this slide's fixture footprint as small as every other slide's in the deck.

slides.title: Equation layout
bullets: Bullets now render above the equation block too
Kept compact so the equations keep most of the slide

equations.caption: photon energy; hbar reduced Planck constant, omega angular frequency
decay rate; tau spontaneous emission lifetime

slides.notes: Demonstrates the equation layout: each equation is rendered by mathimg.py to a cached PNG keyed by a hash of its LaTeX source, then placed as a picture with its caption beneath it, up to three equations per slide as the schema allows. The pptx and html renderers must locate the same cached file independently -- the Node renderer computes the identical sha256-based hash itself rather than shelling out to Python -- so this slide also exercises that cross-language cache-key agreement. Two short textbook-style equations are used here, a photon-energy relation and a decay-rate relation, each with a caption naming every symbol that is not already defined elsewhere on the slide, matching the schema's captioning rule. A schema-wide rule change now also requires bullets to render on every layout that carries them, including this one, so this slide adds two short framing bullets above the equation block -- rendered in a smaller, compact font so the equations still keep most of the vertical space -- to exercise that new rule in both renderers alongside the existing equation-caching path.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Two-column layout

columns.heading: Left column
bullets: First point on the left
Second point on the left

columns.heading: Right column
bullets: First point on the right
Second point on the right

slides.notes: Demonstrates the two-column layout: each column has its own heading and its own bullet list, laid out side by side with equal width and a modest gap between them, useful for comparisons -- before and after, two regimes, two device geometries -- where neither side is more important than the other. Both renderers must divide the available width evenly across however many columns the slide declares, since the schema does not fix the column count at exactly two, and both must keep each column's bullets independent so that one column overflowing does not push text into its neighbor. This fixture keeps both columns short and symmetric on purpose, just enough content to prove the split works correctly.

slides.title: Table layout
slides.notes: Demonstrates the table layout: a header row plus data rows, rendered as a native table in the pptx (so it stays editable and accessible in PowerPoint) and as a plain HTML table on the web page, wrapped in a scrollable container so a wide table never forces the whole page to scroll sideways on a narrow screen. The header row is filled with the section's accent color and white text in both renderers, and body rows alternate a light and white background in the pptx to keep long rows readable, mirroring how a real table of device regimes, fit parameters, or comparison numbers would be presented in the talk, without any of the surrounding renderer code treating this fixture's rows as special cases.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Section Divider
slides.subtitle: A full-bleed break between sections
slides.notes: Demonstrates the section-divider layout: a full-color break slide carrying just a title and an optional subtitle, used between major sections of the two-hour talk to give the audience a visual reset and a moment to see where the talk is headed next. The background fills with the section's accent color rather than white, and both the title and subtitle switch to light text so they stay readable against that dark or saturated background -- a detail both renderers must handle correctly, since every other layout in this fixture assumes a white background and dark ink, and this is the one layout in the whole schema that deliberately inverts that contrast, a detail this fixture exists specifically to catch if either renderer regresses it.

slides.title: Data-driven slides keep four concurrent writers from stepping on one renderer's toes.
slides.subtitle: Demo callout -- no attribution, schema-conformance fixture only
slides.notes: Demonstrates the quote layout: the title field is shown large, centered, and in italics as the quoted text itself, with the subtitle field, if present, shown smaller beneath it as an attribution or a short caption line, the way a pull-quote breaks up a long stretch of technical slides with a single memorable sentence. This fixture's quote is itself a description of why the presentation is built this way -- four workers editing four section files concurrently, all rendered by one shared pair of renderers -- rather than a real citation, and the sources field says so explicitly so nobody mistakes it for an attributed remark from the literature, keeping this fixture honest about its own synthetic origin.

slides.title: Provenance footnote demo
bullets: This slide carries a repo_numbers entry
The renderer prints it as a small provenance footnote
The validator checks the value against the named file
slides.notes: Demonstrates repo_numbers, both forms described in SCHEMA.md: (a) a literal value, checked by validate_sections.py against out/rt_edge/verdict.md, which must contain that value as a numeric token within a relative tolerance of one part in a million; and (b) two computed values, each checked by evaluating a 'how' python expression in a subprocess with the repository root on sys.path, then comparing the result to 'value' within its tolerance, one at the default 1e-6 relative and one relaxed to 1e-3 for a case sensitive to floating-point rounding. Both renderers print a small italic provenance footnote in the slide footer citing every repo_numbers key and its source file, so a reader can trace any number on the slide back to the code or data that produced it.

slides.title: Equation + figure layout
bullets: Bullets now render above the equation column here too
The figure column keeps its full width and height

equations.caption: second-order coherence at zero delay; n photon-number operator

figure.caption: The same sample figure, paired with the equation it illustrates

slides.notes: Demonstrates the new equation+figure layout: an equation block sits on the left half of the slide and the referenced figure sits on the right half, each with its own caption, so a formula and the plot or diagram it produces can share one slide without one crowding out the other. This layout exists because several real sections pair a derived expression directly with a numerical or measured curve that illustrates it, and forcing that pairing across two separate slides -- one equation layout, one figure layout -- would break the narrative flow a lecturer wants when explaining where a formula comes from and what it predicts next. The fixture reuses the sample figure and a short two-photon-coherence equation purely to exercise this new code path in both renderers. A schema-wide rule change now also requires bullets to render on every layout that carries them, including this one, so this slide adds two short bullets above the equation column, in a compact font, while the figure column keeps its full height untouched.
sources: Synthetic demo content -- schema-conformance fixture, not a literature citation.

slides.title: Bullets + table layout
bullets: A short framing statement above a compact table
Bullets take a modest share of the body height
The table gets the rest, so rows stay readable
slides.notes: Demonstrates the new bullets+table layout: a short list of bullets sits above a compact table, useful when a slide needs a few sentences of framing before presenting the numbers -- what regime the table covers, what units or definitions apply, why the comparison matters -- without the bullets and the table competing for the full slide height the way stacking a bullets slide and a table slide separately would require. The bullets get a modest fraction of the body height and the table gets the rest, keeping both legible rather than shrinking the table to fit underneath a full bullets layout. This fixture reuses the same regime-versus-ideality table as the plain table layout above, purely to exercise the new combined layout in both renderers end to end.
